parameters.content:
## 1 · Intake
Two doors in: a form for account managers, and the API intake workflow (validates the request, answers 202 or 400, then calls this one). Both become the same normalized request.

## 2 · Tracker, client profile, AI draft
Every request gets a Notion page first (with its priority), so nothing is lost. Then the client's profile (brand voice, words to avoid, hashtags, account manager) comes from the Notion Clients database; if it can't be read, the draft is written from the request alone. The model must return JSON; if it doesn't, it gets one more try. Brand checks: length per platform, hashtags, words to avoid, the client's hashtags.

## 3 · Human review
The draft and the checks go to #content-review with a link to the review form. The execution waits (no polling) until someone approves, asks for changes (loops back to the AI with the feedback, up to MAX_REVISIONS) or rejects. No answer in time -> the account manager is asked to step in.

## 4 · Schedule + close the loop
Approved posts go to the scheduling tool; the tracker and Slack are updated with the post ID and who approved it.

## 5 · Failures
Every external call retries (3 tries). If a step still fails, the request is marked Failed in Notion, #ops-alerts gets the step, the error and a link to the execution, and the execution is marked failed. The separate Error workflow catches anything unexpected; it skips errors already alerted here ('[handled]').
